hints.title: Recursive Step Branching Obstacle
hints.text: Each step can only be reached from one or two steps below. If you compute all distinct step sequences independently from scratch, duplicate subtrees cause exponential recomputation. How can the solution build directly from the previous two step counts?

hints.title: Two-Term Recurrence Invariant
hints.text: The number of distinct ways to reach step n is the sum of ways to reach step n-1 and ways to reach step n-2, requiring only the two preceding counts.

hints.title: Constant-Space Iteration Procedure
hints.text: Handle base cases: return 1 for 1 step and 2 for 2 steps. Initialize two variables representing the ways to reach the prior two steps. Loop from step 3 up to n, updating the total as their sum and shifting the two variables forward. Return the final accumulated count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterates strictly N times updating two scalar variables.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Uncached recursion branches twice at every step, yielding O(2^N) time and overflowing for N >= 40.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking only the two most recent values achieves optimal O(1) space rather than maintaining an O(N) array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing equivalence to Fibonacci sequence, reduction from O(N) space to O(1) space.
